H1.title: Alpha#30 family: volume-scaled fade of the multi-day up/down streak
H1.source: TARGET.md SEEDS (Kakushadze #30); MEMORY/FINDINGS 2026-10-06 b2 H1; OBSERVATIONS #1, #3
H1.question: Does a cross-sectional fade of the recent streak, scaled by short/long volume, predict next 1h/6h/24h returns across the 10 coins, and is the C3 fade only the response switch?
H1.hypothesis: a change in the 3-day sign-streak rank of Binance daily closes, scaled by sum(volume,5)/sum(volume,20), predicts the cross-sectional rank of the next 24h return of primary price (down-streak + volume surge = higher return) because forced sellers/volume-driven overreaction mean-revert
H1.forbids: no positive rank IC at any horizon on any fold when scored against the pre-2022 (Binance-print) response; if the effect is real it must not vanish when the response is held on the Binance close in C2/C3
H1.rivals: volume ratio alone (attention) ; trailing 1-day reversal ; the Binance-print/FTMO-mid response switch ; hour-of-day clock
H1.anchor: MEMORY b2 H1 posterior 0.85 on C1 +0.037, C2 +0.048 but EXPLORE -0.007 and C3 +0.001 (4 folds, 2 supported): base 0.30 x1.2 for a replicated-in-two-folds seed -> 0.35

H2.title: Alpha#54 family: closing strength (close location x open/close^5) continues
H2.source: TARGET.md SEEDS (-Kakushadze #54); MEMORY/FINDINGS 2026-10-06 b2 H6; OBSERVATIONS #1, #6
H2.question: Does closing strength within the day (close near the high, weighted by (open/close)^5) continue into the next 1h/6h/24h, in rank across the coins?
H2.hypothesis: a change in the daily close-location value times (open/close)^5 of Binance prices predicts the cross-sectional rank of the next 24h return of primary price (higher = continues) because intraday buying pressure that closes near the high is not fully absorbed by the close
H2.forbids: no positive rank IC on any horizon across any anchor hour; an effect that flips sign between the first and second half of EXPLORE is a regime story, not a feature
H2.rivals: same-day return itself (CLV is a transform of the day move); intraday range/vol; response switch; hour-of-day clock
H2.anchor: MEMORY b2 H6 posterior 0.49 (C2 +0.057, C3 +0.023, but EXPLORE halves +0.096/-0.078): base 0.30, no trust uplift for an unstable sign -> 0.30

H3.title: Vol-scaled short-horizon reversal/momentum, market-residual
H3.source: OBSERVATIONS #2, #3, #4, #11; MEMORY already-explored (daily TS reversal, same-hour-yesterday 1h reversal, 6h-block reversal)
H3.question: After removing the BTC/market beta component, is the trailing k-hour return scaled by trailing volatility a cross-sectional predictor, and at what lookback does reversal turn into momentum?
H3.hypothesis: a change in the trailing 1h/3h/6h/12h/24h/72h/168h return of a coin, net of beta x BTC return and divided by its trailing volatility, predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 1h/6h/24h return (negative at short lookbacks, positive at long) because liquidity-driven overshoot reverts while slower information diffuses
H3.forbids: no lookback shows a rank IC beyond min_useful in either direction on the pooled TRAIN; no change with lookback (a flat IC profile) would say the cross-section is pure noise at these horizons
H3.rivals: bid-ask bounce in the Binance print vs the FTMO mid response (OBSERVATIONS #1); volatility level (high-vol coins are the extreme ranks); a BTC lead-lag; the hour-of-day vol clock
H3.anchor: MEMORY: 1h and 6h reversal reached CONFIRM-IC -0.03..-0.06 on earlier runs (pre-v3.3, half its size threshold); tracker base 0.30 x1.3 for repeated sign across runs -> 0.40

H4.title: Volume, trade-count and taker-flow surprises (spot order flow)
H4.source: OBSERVATIONS #3, #5, #13; MEMORY already-explored (reversal after panel volume-shock days; high-volume winners continue)
H4.question: Do surprises in a coin's own quote volume, trade count, average trade size or taker-buy share (vs its trailing norm) predict its next-hour/6h/24h cross-sectional rank?
H4.hypothesis: a change in a coin's quote volume, trade count, average trade size or taker-buy imbalance relative to its trailing 30-day norm predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 1h/6h/24h return because informed or forced flow shows up in size and aggressor side before price fully adjusts
H4.forbids: no volume, trade-count, size or taker-imbalance surprise shows a rank IC beyond min_useful once its interaction with the same-period return is controlled
H4.rivals: the same-period return itself (signed volume is a transform of return); volatility (volume tracks |ret|, corr 0.26); the 5x C3 trade-count regime shift (OBSERVATIONS #5); hour-of-day volume clock
H4.anchor: tracker base 0.30 at ~30% trust for a first look at order-flow features; MEMORY: high-volume winners continue opposite sign on CONFIRM (LOW) -> no uplift -> 0.30

H5.title: Perp positioning: funding, basis rank, open-interest and long/short changes
H5.source: OBSERVATIONS #7, #8, #9; MEMORY already-explored (perp premium cross-section 72h underperformance: sign negative on C1/C2/C3, shrinking)
H5.question: Do cross-sectional ranks of funding, perp-spot basis (premium index), open-interest change and long/short ratio predict the next 1h/6h/24h return rank across coins?
H5.hypothesis: a change in a coin's rank of funding rate / perp premium / open-interest growth / account long-short ratio predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 24h return (crowded long = lower return) because leveraged crowding is unwound and paid for through funding
H5.forbids: no positioning variable has the predicted (negative) sign with an IC beyond min_useful in C2 and C3 together; coverage is only C2+C3 for 9 coins (OBSERVATIONS #9), so a sign-flip between them refutes
H5.rivals: past return (basis and funding follow the trailing return, OBSERVATIONS #8); volatility; the response switch; the pinned funding floor (OBSERVATIONS #7)
H5.anchor: MEMORY perp-premium XS: negative sign on all three folds but EXPLORE effect shrank 85% (OPEN 0.32); coverage limits power: base 0.30 x0.85 -> 0.25

H6.title: Cross-venue gap and lead-lag (Coinbase and Upbit vs Binance)
H6.question: Does a coin's Coinbase-minus-Binance return gap, or its Upbit (Asia-hours) return, lead the next Binance/primary return?
H6.hypothesis: a change in the 1h/6h return gap between a coin's Coinbase (or Upbit) close and its Binance close predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 1h/6h/24h primary return because the venue that is slower to arbitrage reveals flow the other venue has not priced
H6.forbids: no venue-gap feature has an IC beyond min_useful; same-hour Coinbase/Binance correlation of 0.994 leaves little room, so a lead-lag larger than the bid-ask noise would be a surprise
H6.rivals: bid-ask bounce differences between venues; the Binance print vs FTMO mid response; stale prints in thin hours; own-coin reversal
H6.anchor: no earlier run on this panel looked at venue gaps; low-prior speculative family: base 0.30 x0.67 for the near-identity of the venues (corr 0.994) -> 0.20

H7.title: UTC day-boundary anchor: sign-streak fade concentrates at the 23:00 anchor / 00-06 UTC window
H7.question: Is the streak-fade IC specific to the UTC day boundary (anchor hour 23, next 6h), and what is the mechanism?
H7.hypothesis: a change in the 3-day sign-streak rank of daily closes measured at the UTC day boundary predicts the cross-sectional rank of the next 6h and 24h primary return (down-streak = higher return) because daily-candle-based flows (funding clock, daily rebalancing, 00:00 UTC liquidity) concentrate the overreaction unwind right after the daily close
H7.forbids: an IC that is the same at every anchor hour (a flat IC-by-anchor profile) or that sits at a non-boundary hour; an effect present only where the response is the Binance print
H7.rivals: volume clock (00 UTC has the highest vol, OBSERVATIONS #6); trailing 24h return alone (reversal); response switch; day-of-week
H7.anchor: cell_01: streak_daily h6 IC +0.039/+0.057/+0.068/+0.029 on EXPLORE/C1/C2/C3 (all positive, t 2.1/2.1/2.0/1.3), pooled t 3.6, but the same feature at the other 23 anchor hours is ~0.008: base 0.30 + uplift for 4/4 same-sign slices (x1.9) -> 0.45

H8.title: Session-conditional 24h reversal: trailing 24h return rank reverses into the 22-07 UTC window, continues into US hours
H8.source: cells/cell_02_result.md (r24-only anchor-23 h6 IC +0.074, t 6.3; anchors 13-16h negative); OBSERVATIONS #6
H8.question: Does the cross-sectional rank of the trailing 24h return predict the next 1h/6h/24h with a sign that depends on the anchor hour (reversal into the Asia night, continuation into US hours)?
H8.hypothesis: a change in the trailing 24h log-return rank of a coin predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 6h primary return negatively when measured at the 21-01 UTC anchors and positively at the 13-16 UTC anchors, because overnight (Asia-session) liquidity is thin and daily overshoots revert while US-session flow continues the day's trend
H8.forbids: an IC of the same sign at all anchor hours (a flat profile) would refute the clock dependence; a profile that is positive only where the response is the Binance print (EXPLORE/C1) would be the response switch
H8.rivals: plain unconditional daily reversal (H3); volatility clock (00 UTC has the highest |ret|); funding settlement at 00/08/16 UTC; weekday
H8.anchor: cell_02: r24-only anchor-23 h6 IC +0.093/+0.040/+0.071/+0.058 on EXPLORE/C1/C2/C3 (4/4 positive, pooled t 6.3) and negative at 13-16h anchors for the streak: base 0.30 x2.5 (4/4 same sign, large t) -> 0.55

H9.title: Session-gated reversal: the bounce-free 3h/24h reversal lives in signals formed 21-06 UTC and is absent for 13-16 UTC signals
H9.source: cells/cell_04_result.md, cells/cell_07_result.md (rev3s h6 ASIA +0.059 t 8.8 vs US -0.005; paired diff +0.064 t 7.0); OBSERVATIONS #6
H9.question: Is the reversal amplitude a function of the signal's UTC hour (Asia night / EU morning / US session), stable across the four folds, and not a copy of the volatility or volume clock?
H9.hypothesis: a change in the 3-hour (lag-1) or 24h return rank of a coin predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 6h primary return negatively when the signal is formed at 21-06 UTC and not at 13-16 UTC because thin overnight liquidity lets order-flow overshoots persist until the next liquid session, while US-session moves are news-driven and do not revert
H9.forbids: an IC at 13-16 UTC equal to that at 21-01 UTC; an amplitude profile that follows the volatility or volume clock (00 UTC and 14-16 UTC are the busiest hours, so a vol-clock story predicts the US hours reverse MORE); a profile present in EXPLORE only
H9.rivals: volatility clock (OBSERVATIONS #6); volume clock; funding settlement at 00/08/16 UTC (hour 0 and 8 are settlement hours); weekday/weekend mix; the Binance-print-vs-mid response switch
H9.anchor: cells 4 and 7: ASIA-minus-US IC +0.064 at h6 (t 7.0), ASIA positive in 4/4 folds (+0.061/+0.046/+0.059/+0.064): base 0.30 x3.5 (4/4 same sign, t 7-9 in pooled; but searched twice on the same TRAIN, so trust x0.8) -> 0.60

H10.title: Trade-count / volume surprise continuation: coins whose recent trade count runs above its 30-day norm outperform over 6-24h
H10.source: cells/cell_08_result.md (nsurp_1 h24 +0.029 t 4.3; 3 of 4 folds positive); OBSERVATIONS #3, #5
H10.question: Does a coin's 1-24h trade-count (or quote-volume) surprise vs its trailing 30-day norm predict a HIGHER 6-24h cross-sectional return rank, beyond what the same-window return and absolute return explain?
H10.hypothesis: a change in a coin's trade count (volume) over the last 1-24 hours relative to its trailing 720h norm predicts a higher cross-sectional rank of its next 6h/24h primary return because rising participation marks information arrival or attention that continues (an attention-driven momentum), unlike the H4 sign (overheating) we pre-stated
H10.forbids: an IC that vanishes after partialling out the same-window signed return and |return| (volume as a transform of the move); a negative sign in 2 or more folds; an effect present only in the C3 trade-count regime
H10.rivals: same-window return and |return| (high-volume winners continue: MEMORY LOW on CONFIRM, opposite sign); volatility; the C3 5x trade-count regime shift (OBSERVATIONS #5); market-wide volume days
H10.anchor: cell_08: nsurp_1 h24 IC +0.033/+0.025/-0.007/+0.046 (3/4 folds positive), pooled t 4.3, volsurp_1 h24 +0.022 (t 3.3), but opposite to the story pre-stated in H4 and C2 negative; MEMORY says an earlier volume-winner continuation had the opposite sign on CONFIRM: base 0.30 x1.5 for 3/4 folds, x0.8 for the post-hoc sign -> 0.35

H11.title: Risk-shape features: trailing volatility, idiosyncratic volatility, MAX/skew and range rank the coins
H11.source: OBSERVATIONS #3, #11 (vol clustering, fat tails); TARGET.md FAMILIES (volatility)
H11.question: Do recent-risk features (volatility, idiosyncratic volatility, maximum 1h return, skewness, 24h range) rank next-1h/6h/24h returns once the persistent coin level is removed?
H11.hypothesis: a change in a coin's trailing 168h volatility, idiosyncratic volatility, maximum hourly return, return skewness or 24h range predicts a LOWER cross-sectional rank of its next 1h/6h/24h primary return because lottery-like, high-risk coins attract speculative demand and are overpriced
H11.forbids: no one-sided risk feature shows a negative rank IC beyond min_useful after within-coin detrending; an IC that shrinks to zero when the coin's own 90-day mean is removed is a coin fixed effect, not a signal
H11.rivals: coin fixed effect (DOGE/SOL are persistently the most volatile; a 10-coin cross-section with 4 years of luck-dominated mean returns); the short-horizon reversal (high-vol coins have the extreme past returns); the vol clock
H11.anchor: no earlier run on this panel looked at risk-shape features; tracker base 0.30 for a standard anomaly x0.85 because a 10-coin cross-section has little room for a risk premium and cell 11 found a fixed-effect trap -> 0.25

H12.title: BTC / market lead-lag through beta: high-beta coins follow the market's last k-hour move with a delay
H12.source: TARGET.md FAMILIES (cross-coin lead-lag; market-wide return conditioning); OBSERVATIONS #4
H12.question: After a BTC (or equal-weight market) move over the last 1-24 hours, do high-beta coins outperform (market up) or underperform (market down) over the next 1-24 hours?
H12.hypothesis: a change in beta_i x (BTC or EW-market return over the last k hours) predicts the cross-sectional rank of coin i's next 1h/6h/24h primary return with a positive sign because information in BTC reaches high-beta alts with a delay
H12.forbids: no lead_k feature shows a positive IC beyond min_useful at any horizon; a negative IC (market reversal times beta) would refute the diffusion story
H12.rivals: market-wide hourly reversal times beta (raw vs market-residual reversal differed by 0.010 at h1, cell 5); the volatility of the market move (large moves make beta dispersion matter more); the response switch
H12.anchor: no earlier run looked at beta-weighted market moves; tracker base 0.30 x0.67 because cross-sectional dispersion from beta alone is small (pairwise corr 0.4-0.84) and market reversal argues the opposite sign -> 0.20

H13.title: Beta-weighted market reversal: after a market-wide move over the last k hours, high-beta coins give back more (the sign-flipped H12)
H13.source: cells/cell_30_result.md (lead_mkt_1 h1 -0.0316 t -12.8; all 24 variants negative)
H13.question: Is the negative IC of beta x market move a reversal (same sign after up and after down moves) or the fixed effect 'high-beta coins underperformed' (opposite signs in the two states)?
H13.hypothesis: a change in the product of a coin's trailing beta and the last k-hour equal-weight market return predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 1h/6h/24h primary return NEGATIVELY in both market-up and market-down states because market-wide moves overshoot and high-beta coins overshoot most
H13.forbids: an IC of opposite sign in the market-up and market-down states (a fixed effect); an IC that is concentrated in one state; an IC that vanishes when the coin's own average of the feature is removed
H13.rivals: coin fixed effect in beta (high-beta alts underperformed BTC/ETH over 2021-2023); the market reversal itself (a market-timing, not a cross-sectional, effect); the response switch
H13.anchor: cell_30: lead_mkt_k negative IC in all 12 mkt variants, 4/4 folds in lead_mkt_1 h1 (-0.037/-0.035/-0.027/-0.021) but fixed-effect rival unresolved: base 0.30 x2 for consistent sign, x0.67 for the unresolved rival -> 0.40

H14.title: Hour-of-day seasonality persistence: a coin's mean return at the upcoming hour of day over the last 20-60 days predicts its next-bar rank
H14.source: TARGET.md FAMILIES (time-of-day / day-of-week interactions); OBSERVATIONS #6; MEMORY same-hour-yesterday 1h reversal (NO-STORY lead, CONFIRM lag-24 IC -0.035)
H14.question: Does the cross-sectional rank of a coin's own average return at the upcoming UTC hour of day (last 20/60 days, drift removed) persist into the next 1h/6h/24h?
H14.hypothesis: a change in a coin's trailing 20-day or 60-day mean return at the same hour of day as the next bar (net of its own drift) predicts the cross-sectional rank of its next 1h/6h/24h primary return positively because intraday flow patterns (regional sessions, funding/settlement flows, scheduled liquidity) recur for each coin
H14.forbids: no season_N form shows a positive IC beyond min_useful after removing the coin drift; MEMORY says the same-hour-yesterday return has a NEGATIVE sign (-0.035), which would refute persistence in favour of reversal
H14.rivals: same-hour-yesterday reversal (MEMORY NO-STORY lead, a 1-observation version of the same statistic); coin fixed effect (the average return of the coin itself); volatility clock (hours with big moves)
H14.anchor: MEMORY: same-hour-yesterday 1h reversal CONFIRM lag-24 IC -0.035 with no story (sign opposite to persistence); tracker base 0.30 x0.67 for the opposing sign -> 0.20

H15.title: Within-bar shape (last-hour microstructure): close location, wicks, bar gap and VWAP deviation of the last bar
H15.source: TARGET.md FAMILIES (price-path shape: close location, gaps between sessions); OBSERVATIONS #1, #2; cells 5-6 (bounce)
H15.question: Do the shape of the last hourly bar (where it closed inside its range, wicks, the gap between its first trade and the previous close, the close vs the bar VWAP) rank the next-hour/6h/24h return once the print at the bar end can no longer be the entry (one-bar entry delay)?
H15.hypothesis: a change in the last bar's close location, body, wicks, open-versus-previous-close gap or close-versus-VWAP deviation predicts the cross-sectional rank of the following bars' returns because the bar's internal order flow (where the aggressive flow ended) is information about pressure that the close print does not fully carry
H15.forbids: no shape feature shows an IC beyond min_useful at the delayed-entry (bounce-free) scoring; an IC present only at the undelayed entry is the Binance last-print bounce (cells 5-6)
H15.rivals: bid-ask bounce of the last print (cells 5-6); the last-hour return itself (the shape variables are transforms of it); the trade-count and taker-imbalance bounce (cell 9: taker_1 contrarian = rev1)
H15.anchor: no earlier run looked at within-bar shape; tracker base 0.30 x0.85 because cells 6 and 9 show the last-print information is bounce at h1 and ~half of the 1-6h reversal dies with a one-bar delay -> 0.25

H16.title: Multi-day range position, drawdown and moving-average distance rank the coins
H16.source: TARGET.md FAMILIES (price-path shape: range position); OBSERVATIONS #2, #11; cell 5 (k=48-168 reversal IC 0.005-0.019 at h1, ~0 at h24)
H16.question: Do the position of the close inside its trailing 3-30 day range, the drawdown from the trailing high, the rally from the trailing low and the distance to the moving average rank the next 1h/6h/24h returns?
H16.hypothesis: a change in a coin's position in its trailing 72h-720h high-low range, drawdown from the high, rally from the low or distance to the moving average predicts a LOWER cross-sectional rank of its next 6h/24h primary return when high (and a higher one when low) because multi-day extremes are partly given back (range mean reversion)
H16.forbids: no position/drawdown/distance feature has a negative IC beyond min_useful at 6h or 24h; positive IC (trend) would refute the mean-reversion claim
H16.rivals: the short-horizon reversal (a coin at its range top just rose: cells 5-6, f001/f002); the coin fixed effect (a coin in a long trend sits at the top of its range for months); volatility
H16.anchor: cell 5 shows the reversal profile falling to ~0 by k=168 at h24; no earlier run tested range position; tracker base 0.30 x0.67 -> 0.20

H17.question: Do the aggressor imbalance of Binance USD-M perpetual trades, its gap to spot, the perp share of dollar volume and the perp trade-count surprise rank the next 1h/6h/24h returns beyond the same-window return?

H17.rivals: bid-ask bounce / own-window return (cell 9: taker_1 residual on rev1 = 0); the premium feature f004 (leveraged longs pay the premium); the coin fixed effect in perp share of volume
